annotationRationale: Both reviewed methods combine unordered-pair counting with integer restrictions from the win ratio. The alternative additionally bounds the player count using forced wins. The historical win-cap route gives an equivalent bound.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Counting & Probability remains appropriate because counting unordered player pairs is central.

review.questionCheck: The reduced win ratio is 7:5, so the game total is divisible by 12. Pair counting and the forced-win bound yield 36 games, realized by three left-handed and six right-handed players with win totals 21 and 15. This agrees with choice B and the key. No figure or statement contradiction is present.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Independently verified the identical source question 2023_AMC_10A_Q16. Its methods 2023_AMC_10A_Q16#screen-the-listed-game-totals and 2023_AMC_10A_Q16#bound-forced-right-handed-wins are both retained and independently complete. The historical route 2023_AMC_10A_Q16#win-cap-bound is merged into the equivalent forced-win bound; 2023_AMC_10A_Q16#screen-listed-totals is merged into the answer-choice route. Those historical entries contain no additional worked explanations. Every useful distinct reviewed shared method is retained.
review.annotationCheck: Unordered-pair counting and integer restrictions are correctly assessed. Percent conversion and division in a ratio are appropriate support concepts. The alternative's linear-inequality node correctly records its additional operation.
review.areaCheck: Counting & Probability remains appropriate because counting unordered player pairs is central.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The reduced ratio forces totals 7k and 5k, hence 12k games. Only 36 and 48 survive. Since 45 and 55 are consecutive possible pair totals, 48 is impossible. The nine-player construction gives 18+3=21 left-handed wins and 15 right-handed wins, verifying feasibility.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: This is explicitly authorized reuse of the reviewed project method, not copied third-party prose. The exact source question and method are identified. Both inherited reference IDs, aops-reference-2023_AMC_10A_Q16 and live-reference-2023_AMC_10A_Q16, are preserved alongside the shared-method reference. No official MAA authorship is claimed.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The explanation justifies integrality using the reduced ratio, derives pair counting without requiring combination notation, and verifies that the surviving choice satisfies the handedness condition.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: The combination, integer-equation, and percentage nodes all match decisive written steps. No modular-congruence node is needed for this divisibility argument.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact native combination-application and percentage links fit the work. Integer-equation reasoning has no accepted CN link supplied. The question-level ratio-distribution support is also appropriate.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: S-CP.B.9 supplies a narrower counting connection, without evidence of compound-probability coverage. The narrower 6.RP.A.3 and 6.RP.A.3c links support percentage reasoning, but this instance does not cover their full demands. Integer restrictions remain an alignment gap.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The direct IDs accurately capture unordered-pair counting, integral win totals, and conversion of 140% to 7/5.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Right-handed internal games force at least l(2l-1) wins. Comparing this with 5T/12 gives 5(3l-1)≥8(2l-1), hence l≤3. The positive integer cases give totals 3, 15, and 36; only 36 is divisible by 12. The construction attains the endpoint l=3.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The exact reviewed project method and identical source question are correctly credited. Its shared reference and both inherited LIVE and AoPS reference IDs are retained. Recasting a maximum-left-win bound as a minimum-right-win bound is mathematically faithful, and source-informed-original is accurate.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The forced-win observation motivates the inequality. The positive division, simplified bound, complete integer cases, and attainable endpoint are all explained sufficiently.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: Pair counting, integer restrictions, percentage conversion, and solving a linear inequality are all present and correctly mapped.
